pastWeek.title: Downtown Street Eats
pastWeek.summary: A weekday food-truck rally in Cadillac Square with rotating trucks and carts—a useful downtown lunch plan when you want choice without committing to a restaurant.

pastWeek.title: The Ark's Open Stage
pastWeek.summary: A warm, low-pressure open stage where performers get eight minutes or two songs; names are drawn at 7:55 and 8:30, and the audience gets a first look at local work.

pastWeek.title: Blind Pig Comedy
pastWeek.summary: A cheap, late, low-stakes local comedy night at the Blind Pig. Buy before heading over; the venue lists this date as 21+.

pastWeek.title: Waterway Relatives
pastWeek.summary: A conversation with U-M professor Selena Smith about resilient water systems, followed by sampling trays, aquatic organisms, and a short walk through Willow Pond's living systems.

pastWeek.title: Game Night and RPG One-Shots
pastWeek.dateLabel: Today, game night 5:00 PM; beginner RPG one-shots at 6:00 PM
pastWeek.summary: A welcoming evening for board games, puzzles, miniature painting, or a beginner-friendly one-session tabletop RPG—exactly the kind of participatory game night this brief should surface.

pastWeek.title: What Do You Carry? Community Showcase & Open Mic
pastWeek.venue: U-M Arts Initiative, 343 S. Fifth Ave.
pastWeek.summary: A community story circle and open mic for poems, songs, reflections, and art about what people carry; attending simply to listen is expressly welcome.

pastWeek.title: Tomato Bonanza
pastWeek.venue: Ann Arbor District Library — Malletts Creek
pastWeek.summary: Lakehouse Bakery owner Keegan Rodgers leads a hands-on tomato-sauce workshop with tasting and useful ideas for garden or market tomatoes.

pastWeek.title: Long Story Short
pastWeek.price: $15 advance; $18 at the door if available
pastWeek.summary: A new true-personal-storytelling night at a brewery-theater, built around a different monthly theme.

pastWeek.title: Lost Mary
pastWeek.price: Free; donations accepted for Food Gatherers
pastWeek.summary: Hillsdale songwriters Luke Martin and David Johnson III bring front-porch folk storytelling, traditional and modern Americana, and an unusually good free listening-room finish to the day.

pastWeek.title: Happy Hour: saahnjoo
pastWeek.summary: A free early set from Detroit-metro solo ambient-pop artist saahnjoo, whose voice, keys and drum machine turn loss, gratitude and hope into a compact listening-room experience.

pastWeek.title: JDs Stage Bistro Opening Celebration
pastWeek.dateLabel: Aug 26–29, shows 7:00 PM; bistro 4:00 PM, stage doors 5:30 PM
pastWeek.price: $75 Aug 26; $100 Aug 27–29; food and drinks separate
pastWeek.registration: Reserved-table ticket required; seating is limited
pastWeek.category: New venue, dining and live music
pastWeek.summary: Jeff Daniels opens a new chef-driven, Michigan-forward restaurant and intimate listening room with four nights featuring a solo set, The War and Treaty, Southern Avenue, and the Ben Daniels Band with Brad Phillips.
pastWeek.deadline: Opening-week seats are limited; book now

pastWeek.title: Open Mic Wednesday with Annie Bacon & Forrest Hejkal
pastWeek.price: $5 cover; nobody turned away for inability to pay
pastWeek.summary: A genuinely mixed-form open mic for songs, stories, poetry, comedy, magic and monologues, hosted by a songwriter and an experience-maker who has turned barns into theaters.

pastWeek.title: Rush — Fifty Something Tour
pastWeek.dateLabel: Wed Aug 26 and Fri Aug 28, 7:30 PM
pastWeek.summary: Geddy Lee and Alex Lifeson celebrate more than 50 years of Rush music and honor Neil Peart in two Detroit arena shows.
pastWeek.deadline: Check remaining seats now; first show is August 26

pastWeek.title: SAW The Musical: The Unauthorized Parody
pastWeek.summary: A deliberately campy musical parody of the first Saw movie, making its Detroit stop for three performances.

pastWeek.title: Sonic Lunch: Mavis Staples with Mei Semones
pastWeek.summary: A rare free lunchtime appearance by Mavis Staples, with inventive guitarist-songwriter Mei Semones opening, in downtown Ann Arbor.

pastWeek.title: Happy Hour: Rachel Arnsdorf
pastWeek.summary: A free happy-hour set from Ann Arbor jazz vocalist Rachel Arnsdorf with pianist Aris Chalin—an easy after-work choice before the neighborhood gets busy.

pastWeek.title: LGBTQ Night: Trivia with Terry McClymonds
pastWeek.summary: A friendly, non-sports game night with verbal and written trivia rounds led by Aut Bar's former longtime trivia host; food and drinks are available, and the club opens at 5 PM.

pastWeek.title: Emus on the Loose: An Emu-sical!
pastWeek.dateLabel: Fri Aug 28, 7:00 PM; Sat Aug 29, noon and 3:00 PM; Sun Aug 30, 3:00 PM
pastWeek.venue: The Village Theater at Cherry Hill
pastWeek.registration: Tickets online or at the box office
pastWeek.summary: A one-hour, locally created musical based on the semi-true story of four runaway emus, expanded into a comic tour of Michigan; Saturday shows add illustrator crafts and snacks.

pastWeek.title: Bluegrass Friday: Pontiac Trail Blazers featuring Tony Pace
pastWeek.summary: Ann Arbor's house bluegrass crew plays traditional standards, originals and left-field covers with Tony Pace adding dobro in a small room.

pastWeek.title: Sal Demilio
pastWeek.dateLabel: Fri Aug 28, 7:15 PM; Sat Aug 29, 7:15 and 9:45 PM
pastWeek.summary: A veteran Michigan club comic with warm, self-deprecating storytelling about family life, Italian culture, technology and everyday absurdity.

pastWeek.title: my salamander
pastWeek.summary: A compact, hard-to-classify set bridging classical, rock, folk and punk, built through an intentionally experimental group process.

pastWeek.title: Ypsi Pride
pastWeek.summary: A long, free Depot Town celebration with drag performances, family activities, food vendors, and room to drop in rather than commit to a single set.

pastWeek.title: Open Board Games
pastWeek.summary: A casual all-afternoon table for learning and playing a wide range of board games; instruction is available, so it works even without a group.

pastWeek.title: Summer Game 2026 Game Over Gala!
pastWeek.summary: A bright, low-pressure celebration for AADL Summer Game players with button making, face painting, coloring, and light refreshments.

pastWeek.title: Emma's Wedding(s)
pastWeek.summary: The final performance of Carey Crim's comedy-drama about friends revisiting three previous weddings before a fourth attempt at 'the one.' Adult language and subject matter.

pastWeek.title: Apples & Honey Fall Festival
pastWeek.summary: A compact Rosh Hashanah celebration with music, dance lessons, workshops, local organizations, food for sale, and David Zinn sidewalk chalk.

pastWeek.title: Dance Day: Terpsichore Collective Fundraiser
pastWeek.summary: Watch a local professional troupe rehearse a new October work, meet the dancers over appetizers, or arrive at 3 PM for the open community dance class.

pastWeek.title: Alonso Umana Quartet
pastWeek.summary: Costa Rican-born, Mexico-raised drummer Alonso Umana leads two Sunday sets in a true small-room jazz club; reserve if you want dinner with the music.

pastWeek.title: BIIRD with Warren & Flick
pastWeek.registration: Tickets online or at the box office
pastWeek.summary: An all-women Irish trad collective brings virtuosic pub-session energy, harp, fiddle, concertina, flute, vocals and drums to the Ark; the venue flags low ticket availability.

today.title: Downtown Street Eats
today.summary: Downtown Detroit's weekday food-truck rally makes an easy lunch wander; today's lineup includes Twisted Street BBQ, Sonny's Hamburgers, Los Dos Amigo's Taco Truck, Gambino's Catering, and Impasto.

today.title: Sewing Lab
today.summary: Bring a project or learn the basics in a welcoming library sewing lab; no prior sewing experience is required.

today.title: Joyful Movement: Zumba Party
today.summary: A beginner-welcoming Zumba party at the library—an easy, no-cost way to move without committing to a studio membership.

today.title: The Hidden Blazers
today.summary: A free three-hour bluegrass set in a downtown cocktail bar; service-industry workers receive 25% off their tabs.

today.title: Opera by the Glass
today.summary: An unusually casual opera night in a brewery: hear singers up close while sampling beer, with reservations required to claim a spot.

today.title: Scottish Country Dancing
today.summary: Tartan Thistle teaches and calls participatory Scottish country dances with live music; arrive in comfortable shoes and no partner is needed.

today.title: The Brudi Brothers with Meels
today.registration: Tickets online or at the box office
today.summary: Three Seattle brothers make warm, bluesy Americana with old-world soul, street-poet wit and sibling harmonies; Meels opens with 'Critter Country' folk, country and bluegrass.

today.title: Blind Pig Comedy
today.summary: A cheap, low-stakes Monday comedy room—especially useful if you want an easy night out rather than a formal ticketed show.

easyAnswer: Tonight, The Ark’s Brudi Brothers are the strong small-room ticket, while Opera by the Glass turns 734 Brewing into a close-up, reservation-only opera night. For low-cost hangs, catch free Hidden Blazers bluegrass at the Ravens Club or $2.50 Blind Pig Comedy. Tomorrow, play free Tacos & Trivia at CABANA 313 or make a food-truck lunch at Cadillac Square.

planAhead.title: Poetry Open Mic with Forrest Hejkal & cat h. bradley

planAhead.title: Comedy Bingo

planAhead.title: Brews, Brats and Bands

planAhead.title: H.O.M.E.S. Project
